title: Rob Citrone – Emerging Markets, Hedge Funds, and Staying in the Game (Capital Allocators, EP.261)

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Rob Citrone – Emerging Markets, Hedge Funds, and Staying in the Game (Capital Allocators, EP.261).docx
meta.transcript source: YouTube auto-captions (no punctuation on this video's captions)

speakers: Rob Citrone (founder, Discovery Capital Management; ex-Tiger, Fidelity, Soros)
summary:
Capital Allocators EP.261 (July 2022) with EM/global macro hedge fund manager Rob Citrone: lessons from Julian Robertson and George Soros (exit fully on lost conviction, cross-reference ideas, how to short), a top-down plus bottom-up process, and mid-2022 views (liquidity withdrawal, China, Russia, Brazil, Argentina, Turkey short, Japan YCC short, Europe).
Conclusions: macro drives ~80% of ideas, EM equities are slowest to react, size shorts small with big skew, avoid crowding and groupthink.

completeness_estimate: 0.82 - first reader captured the Tiger/Soros lessons, short-selling rules, process, and nearly all 2022 market views with accurate numbers; missed India, Africa, the Brady bond and Turkey-1999 examples, the network/information edge, the fee give-back alignment point and two H2-2022 swing factors.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: the fed came in and just eased liquidity massively it was an interesting time to buy obviously and we could see that and feel that that's why things recovered very quickly
claims.claim: After the 1987 crash the Fed eased liquidity massively and markets recovered quickly, so heavy liquidity injection marked a buying opportunity.
claims.direction: long equities after crash with central bank liquidity
claims.conditions: when the central bank can ease

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: even if the market will crash there's not much the fed can do because of the inflation issue
claims.claim: In 2022 the Fed cannot rescue markets as in 1987 because inflation forces it to tighten and withdraw liquidity.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: as we take three trillion out it has to have a significant impact on asset prices in my view
claims.claim: If QE added trillions to asset prices, the second phase of the 2022 correction is quantitative tightening liquidity withdrawal, which has not yet started to bite.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: so many people have huge amounts of their wealth in the market especially united states and so i think this is going to have a much bigger impact on the economy
claims.claim: Broader household equity ownership (401ks) makes a market correction transmit more strongly to the economy than in 1987, so a substantial slowdown is likely.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: we think core inflation's peaked we think it's going to come down but unfortunately it's not going to come down fast enough where the fed can stop
claims.claim: Core inflation peaked in mid-2022 after three monthly declines but will not fall fast enough to stop Fed tightening; energy and food are headline risks.
claims.indicator: core CPI year over year and month over month

correction.issue: Citrone says core inflation has fallen three months in a row year over year (and also month over month), not three monthly declines.
correction.fix: Core inflation peaked in mid-2022: three straight year-over-year declines plus lower month-over-month readings, but it will not fall fast enough to let the Fed stop tightening; energy and food are the headline risks.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: we have all our debt in our own currency so we can actually print the money which we've done in the past and we're actually inflating our debt away right now
claims.claim: Because US debt is in its own currency and the dollar is the reserve currency, the US avoids EM-style currency-to-debt crises; inflation, not debt, is the issue.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: we were short japan along the us and that was a massive macro trade
claims.claim: Tiger's decade-long macro trade was short Japan (Nikkei from 40,000 to 9,000) and long US in the 1990s, held through thick and thin.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: we'd lose 10 in japanese equities because they would always ramp the equities into the end of the quarter at their fiscal year end of march
claims.claim: Japanese equities were ramped into quarter-end/March fiscal year end, hurting shorts; the short was lightened early in the quarter and re-added at the end.
claims.direction: lighten shorts early, add before quarter end
claims.conditions: at quarter-end and March fiscal year end

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: when they lost conviction and idea they got out they didn't wait around they didn't get half the position out they just got out of the position and they took whatever the market price was
claims.claim: Julian Robertson and George Soros exited a position fully at market when conviction was lost instead of waiting for a better price, because waiting tends to lead to worse exits.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: they always cross reference their ideas
claims.claim: Both top investors cross-checked every idea with outside people, who else knows or holds a view; this reduces idea error.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: we had these friday lunches where we had to come in with an idea that we wanted to present and also an idea we want to take out of the portfolio
claims.claim: Tiger required analysts to present one idea to add and one to remove each week, forcing preparation and debate.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: georgia's a big problem in eastern europe and if eastern europe comes down then western european bank's going to go down
claims.claim: In the 2008 crisis Eastern Europe's problems would cascade through Western European bank lending; a lender standstill plus IMF program was proposed.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: you've got to be incredibly careful because there's unlimited loss in shorts you don't want to ever have any of the shorts too large
claims.claim: Shorts have unlimited loss so size must stay small, and shorts should be chosen where skew is heavily favourable (risk 10-15, make 75-80).

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: you also want to have shorts that the skew is so much in your favor like if you're long you lose 10 or 15 if you're right you make 75 or 80
claims.claim: Tiger's best shorts had payoff skew: the Thai baht short in 1997 went about 40% in favour despite a loss of 225 million along the way, because unsustainable rates and no reserves made the peg unsustainable.
claims.indicator: FX reserves; interest rate level vs peg
claims.direction: short currencies with depleted reserves and unsustainable pegs

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: julian would always say well the best shorts go down ninety percent they don't get them 40 or 50 they go down 90
claims.claim: Once a broken short is working keep the position, the best shorts fall about 90% (Thai baht, China red chips with hidden debt, Mexican builders) not 40-50%.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: i think the best shorts are ones where there's either a fundamental flaw in the business model or is ultimately going to go bankrupt
claims.claim: Distinguish shorts with catalysts that fall 30-40% from broken business models heading to bankruptcy; conviction should stay high on the latter even at lower prices.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: we generate probably 80 of our ideas from our macro side of things but then we can populate them with securities that are much more efficient using the bottom up analysis
claims.claim: Process: about 80% of ideas come from macro analysts, and bottom-up stock analysts pick the efficient securities; technology expertise is also needed.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: the equity markets are really the most inefficient markets they tend not to react as quickly as the currency or the debt
claims.claim: In EM, equities react more slowly than currencies and debt, so macro signals can be exploited in equities, often via country baskets (e.g. short the five or six best banks).

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: turkey cds has gone from about 400 overnight to 800 over we think it's going well over a thousand
claims.claim: Turkey is the best short in 2022: CDS 400 to 800, reserves negative about 50bn, deposits spent, inflation 70-80%, so a currency and credit crisis is expected.
claims.direction: short Turkey currency, banks, buy CDS

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: i start by thinking about what do i think overall about the markets and risk in general
claims.claim: Portfolio construction starts from the view on equities, dollar and rates direction, then positions are populated where weakness or strength is.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: i think china is going to ultimately become uninvestable market
claims.claim: China is potentially uninvestable due to a leader focused on power rather than growth, with over 30% of the EM equity index and much foreign money stuck; short CNH and equities tempered by about 15% odds Xi loses a second term.
claims.conditions: depends on Oct 2022 People's Congress outcome

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: we're in a process of moving to a massive cold war of the west against china and russia i think that's terrible for returns
claims.claim: A cold war of the West against China and Russia is bad for returns and assets prices.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: there's an opportunity investment of a lifetime in russian assets
claims.claim: If Russia undergoes regime change, depressed Russian assets (1/99th of previous prices, as in 1998) could return about 50 times quickly, so a small allocation is a lifetime option.
claims.direction: long Russian assets on regime change

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: i think is now unfortunately going to reverse and i think this is going to be lower growth higher inflation
claims.claim: Globalisation is reversing, implying lower growth and higher inflation.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: you can try in the u.s at three and a half percent rates or you can go to brazil where they're 14 instead of 100 basis points you can make 800 basis points
claims.claim: Brazil offers rate-cut upside (rates 14%), equities and currency carry (12% net yield) as political risk is stable in the 2022 election; Argentina could be best market next year after market-oriented election change.
claims.direction: long Brazil bonds, currency; long Argentina

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: there's no way that's going to hold in this environment that's one of the best fixed income shorts in the world today
claims.claim: Japan's yield curve control cap at 25 bps cannot hold with global inflation; short JGBs, long end gains of 50-75 bps; developed sovereign bonds were shorts generally.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: anytime a company's still being priced to sales or they're talking about the tam i want nothing to do with that company probably a short
claims.claim: Tech companies valued on price to sales or TAM talk are shorts; multiples are too high and more pain was expected in 2022-23.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: usually travel is terrible in a recession i think it's going to do very well because there's so much pent-up demand there
claims.claim: Expect a mild US and global recession by early 2023 in which travel does well because of pent-up demand.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: europe is in serious trouble and this ukraine russian situation has just made it worse
claims.claim: Europe heads toward recession with 14 differing national policies, an energy shock, and possible accident in 18-24 months.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: ultimately there's gonna be a fantastic short in italian debt
claims.claim: Short Italian debt ahead of next year's election and short the DAX (no energy firms, heavy industrial exposure, natural gas six times US prices).

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: we have probably about 10 themes on at a time and then each of those themes may have 10 to 15 positions
claims.claim: Portfolio structure: about 10 themes with 10-15 positions each, 120-150 positions, baskets counted as one position.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: we'll get to 20 25 net short if we really get incredibly concerned
claims.claim: Net exposure goes up to 20-25% net short in equities; credit risk is about half and currency about a third of equity volatility.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: grew too fast too many people i diluted our ideas
claims.claim: At peak $15bn the fund diluted ideas; it will not return to that size because the markets' liquidity is worse than 10-15 years ago.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: it's really important to try to not get group think within the organization
claims.claim: Cross-reference ideas with outside contacts (policymakers, consultants, other managers), as more people in the firm reduce time for outside checking.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: central banks talk a lot to each other i never really understood how much they do speak to each other especially now through the bis
claims.claim: Central banks coordinate and share ideas via the BIS, so policymaker contacts help anticipate their stances.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: that crowding issues not anything that i see is an issue anymore
claims.claim: Crowding was a bigger issue when the fund was large (2013-15); a smaller, eclectic EM-heavy book has few names shared with other hedge funds.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: the worst analyst is the one who just gets dug in his position
claims.claim: Good analysts change their mind when facts change and constantly replace good ideas with better ideas.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: positions were too big we're betting on regulatory things the size in terms of liquidity we want to change our mind it made it very difficult to reduce the position
claims.claim: In 2019 two large positions on US regulatory decisions went wrong; positions were too big (about 10-15 of the portfolio) and illiquid, making reduction hard.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: it's possible the markets may bottom the next six or seven months but probably much lower levels than here
claims.claim: Markets may bottom in six to seven months but at much lower levels, with a tough next 18 months.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: time to me is a continuum and i don't think about it in short-term months or days or weeks
claims.claim: Short-term focus is the investment pet peeve; it is impossible to manage money on a short-term basis.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: they were restructuring a lot of the latin american debt in the brady bonds and we got involved in buying some of this debt and the yields were 25 in dollars these things performed incredibly well
claims.claim: Buying restructured Latin American sovereign debt (Brady bonds) after the 1980s debt crisis offered about 25% dollar yields and performed very well as the region boomed in the early 1990s: post-crisis restructured EM debt is a rich entry point.
claims.direction: long restructured EM sovereign debt after a crisis
claims.conditions: after debt restructuring and into a recovery

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: it was maybe the biggest development in the history of the world but it's going to be the biggest disaster and the losses are going to be enormous and then a year later it's completely populated
claims.claim: Citrone's early view that Shanghai's Pudong high-rises were a ghost-town disaster was wrong within a year because the state brought people in, an analogy that state-directed development can fill apparent overbuild and that vacancy alone is a poor basis for a China bear case.
claims.indicator: vacancy in newly built Chinese districts
claims.conditions: state ability to direct population and investment

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: i think now it's a time to be sure that individual stocks has been for the last few months and i think that's going to continue for a while
claims.claim: In mid-2022 Citrone thinks individual stock shorts (captions garble 'sure' for 'short') have been working for months and will keep working, in a market where single-stock short selling is a lost art.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: my rolodex into these local key players and a lot of cases policymakers a lot of these countries is very important
claims.claim: A personal network of local players and policymakers, built over decades of country trips, lets Citrone get up to speed fast when a long-dormant market (Latin America) becomes interesting; keeping coverage of out-of-favour markets lets him switch long or short quickly.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: two things i'd love to know about the rest of the year one is what happened to ukraine russian war which i still think remain a quagmire
claims.claim: The two swing factors Citrone identifies for the rest of 2022 are whether the Ukraine war is resolved (still a quagmire; a resolution would be a big market event) and who leads China after the autumn party congress.
claims.indicator: Ukraine war outcome; China leadership decision

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: we think india will be the new growth country of the world they've done a lot of reforms over a long period of time
claims.claim: India is Citrone's long-term growth favourite: decades of reform, a large market, English language and good rule of law make reforms hard to reverse, with key-person political risk around Modi.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: i think you can play them through western companies that have operations in africa and that's probably the best way to play it
claims.claim: African commodity strength is hard to capture directly because of political chaos and weak governance, so Citrone prefers Western companies with African operations and sees little to buy in South Africa.
claims.direction: long Western firms with African operations rather than local assets

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: the turkish equity market in the month of december in our fifth month doubled the market doubled the whole market doubled we made 22 that month on a net basis
claims.claim: After the 1998 Russian crisis, EM equities can rebound violently (Turkey's market doubled in December 1999, +22% net for the fund) while investors ignore them to chase a bubble (Nasdaq), so crisis-lows entry in EM is highly asymmetric.
claims.direction: long EM equities after a crisis

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: the close of europe i see the open of age it really gives me an edge i can feel what the markets are doing a little bit
claims.claim: Following markets around the clock (European close, Asian open) through a 24-hour trading desk gives Citrone a feel for market direction and some trading edge.

claims.speaker: Rob Citrone
claims.quote: anybody who stays i'm going to give credit back your management fees instead of closing down
claims.claim: After a bad year Discovery credited back management fees to investors who stayed instead of closing and relaunching to reset the high-water mark, and investors recovered losses and more in under two years: fee give-backs and refusal to reset are alignment signals when choosing hedge fund managers.
claims.indicator: manager fee and high-water-mark behaviour after losses
